item.title: Ba FA will not comment on social media speculation surrounding former coach – Dayal
item.description: Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the association is aware of social media discussions surrounding former coach Ravinesh Kumar, but it does not engage in public speculation or comment on social media rumours. This is after the Association announced the termination of Kumar's contract, effective immediately.
item.content:encoded:
Ba Football Association President Praneel Dayal says the association is aware of social media discussions surrounding former coach Ravinesh Kumar, but it does not engage in public speculation or comment on social media rumours.

This is after the Association announced the termination of Kumar's contract, effective immediately.

Dayal confirmed to fijivillage News that the association will not be making any further comments on the matter.

He says all internal matters handled by the Ba Football Association are addressed through its established procedures and guidelines.

Dayal says internal administrative processes and confidential personnel matters are handled by the executive leadership, and the association will not discuss internal operational details publicly.

The President says internal employment matters remain confidential to protect the privacy of all parties involved.

He says the association has addressed the matter internally and moved forward in its best interests.

Dayal says their focus remains strictly on managing the association responsibly and maintaining the standards expected by their community .

He says the Ba Football Association has a robust organisational structure and a clear technical pathway.

When asked who is being considered as the new coach, given that the team needs to prepare for the Champions vs Champions and OFC Champions League, Dayal says their preparations and standards for upcoming commitments remain fully intact.

He further says the Executive Committee is currently evaluating coaching options, and an official announcement regarding technical appointments will be made once the process is complete.

Dayal adds that, as stated in their release, the association's internal standards and organisational values are non-negotiable.

We have also reached out to Kumar for his response.

item.title: 17-year-old Tabete focused on mindset ahead of Youth Olympic Games
item.description: Maintaining the right mindset and persevering through challenges are among the biggest difficulties faced by 17-year-old Roko Ilaisa Tabete as he prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal. Tabete, who is from Yaroi in Matuku, Lau, will represent Fiji in triathalon.
item.content:encoded:
Maintaining the right mindset and persevering through challenges are among the biggest difficulties faced by 17-year-old Roko Ilaisa Tabete as he prepares to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal.

Tabete, who is from Yaroi in Matuku, Lau, will represent Fiji in triathalon.

He says competing in track and field requires an individual mindset and the determination to keep going through difficult times.

The International School Suva student says he copes by singing songs in his head and talking to fellow athletes during training, as having people around him helps him improve.

Tabete says preparations for the Games are going well, with a focus on technical and physical training.

He says representing Fiji is both an honour and a privilege, having previously represented the country in track and field and basketball.

Tabete has thanked fans for their support and says he hopes to represent Fiji with pride at the Games.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.

item.title: 16-year-old Josaia Croker excited to represent Fiji at Youth Olympic Games
item.description: 16-year-old Josaia Croker of Rotuma says it is an honour and privilege to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal as he balances his triathlon training with his schoolwork. The Marist Brothers High School student says his preparations for the Games are going well, despite the challenges of managing his academic commitments alongside his sporting ambitions.
item.content:encoded:
16-year-old Josaia Croker of Rotuma says it is an honour and privilege to represent Fiji at the 2026 Youth Olympic Games in Dakar , Senegal as he balances his triathlon training with his schoolwork.

The Marist Brothers High School student says his preparations for the Games are going well, despite the challenges of managing his academic commitments alongside his sporting ambitions.

He says one of the biggest sacrifices he has had to make as a young athlete is spending less time with his friends so he can focus on training and studying .

Croker says his family has been very supportive of his journey and is helping him as he prepares to compete on the international stage.

He says he is excited about the opportunity to represent Fiji and is grateful for the chance to achieve this milestone at just 16 years old.

The 2026 Youth Olympic Games will be held in Dakar, Senegal, from 30th October to 13th November.
